findings.text: The scan selects every JSON file under the review store with no de-duplication, and the store leaves byte-identical duplicates (the head-keyed copy beside the legacy path, and re-stores under a second run identity): 161 of 835 selected files at review time, 153 of 820 at capture, duplicate another selected file's exact bytes, so the headline 820 record count is 667 distinct records and every absolute count is inflated by about 19%.

The repair criterion is satisfied by a duplicate file of the same review: records are ordered by the review record's own timestamp and a duplicate carries the identical stamp, so the twin reads as a later finding-bearing review of the same implement run; nine duplicate pairs carry opposite repair flags, and file-level repairs exceed distinct repaired reviews.

The record pins no corpus revision and names measurement.log as an output while that log is zero bytes, so nothing on disk attests the gate the manifest claims; a re-run of the same script bytes at review time returns 835 records, 707 finding-bearing and 172 repairs, and no pinned state lets a reader reconcile that against the reported 820, 692 and 171.
